oewn-01366351-v.learner: To coat, cover, or smear a surface with something.
examples: She applied a thin coat of paint to the old door.

oewn-02565990-v.learner: To make sure that laws and rules are obeyed.
examples: The referee applied the rules strictly to both teams.

oewn-02601520-v.learner: To set yourself to work at something and give it your effort.
examples: If he applied himself to his studies, he would pass easily.

oewn-01028567-v.learner: To use a word or name for a person or thing.
examples: The critics applied the word "genius" to her.

oewn-02567247-v.learner: To make use of something for yourself.
examples: He tries to apply the principle of honesty in his own life.

oewn-02713289-v.learner: To be able to be used on something, in the way an analysis can be used on a case.
examples: This way of reading applies well to short poems.

oewn-02314145-v.learner: To give or pass something on in a physical way.
examples: Apply firm pressure to the cut until it stops bleeding.

oewn-07227272-n.learner: A message, usually written, given ahead of time to say that you mean to leave an arrangement or contract.
examples: She gave her landlord a month's notice before she moved out.

oewn-06806283-n.learner: A sign put up in a public place to advertise something.
examples: A notice in the shop window offered rooms to let.

oewn-06422419-n.learner: A short review that judges how good something is.
examples: The new play got good notices in the papers.

oewn-07200328-n.learner: A request asking someone to pay money.
examples: The bank sent him a notice asking him to pay what he owed.

oewn-14334775-n.learner: A sign or feeling in the body that is caused by an illness or a drug.
examples: Sleepiness is a common effect of this medicine.

oewn-04816894-n.learner: The state of a law being legally valid.
examples: The new law comes into effect next month.

oewn-06616419-n.learner: The main meaning or theme of a speech or a piece of writing.
examples: She said something to the effect that she was tired of waiting.

oewn-01065717-v.learner: To ask for someone or something to take part or to be present.
examples: All parents are invited to the school meeting on Friday.

oewn-01763987-v.learner: To make something more likely to happen.
examples: Leaving your door unlocked invites trouble.

oewn-01472399-v.learner: To ask someone to come in.
examples: She opened the door and invited him in.

oewn-01472854-v.learner: To show that you are willing to have someone in your home or the area around you.
examples: The little town invited new families to settle there.

oewn-02390082-v.learner: To have someone as your guest.
examples: He invited her to dinner at the new restaurant.

oewn-00169266-v.learner: To change your clothes; to put on different clothes.
examples: She went upstairs to change before dinner.

oewn-00161033-v.learner: To swap or replace something with another, usually one of the same kind.
examples: We had to change the flat tyre by the side of the road.

oewn-00551194-v.learner: To put aside, give up, or leave one thing for another.
examples: He changed sides halfway through the argument.

oewn-02262178-v.learner: To give something to each other and receive something from each other.
examples: Would you change seats with me?

oewn-02092508-v.learner: To get off one vehicle or transport line and onto another.
examples: We had to change trains at York.

oewn-00163059-v.learner: To take off or replace the coverings of something.
examples: She changes the beds every Monday.
His voice began to change when he was thirteen.

oewn-08661788-n.learner: A place where it is not safe to be.
examples: The soldiers pulled the wounded man out of danger.

oewn-07406116-n.learner: A sudden loud bang, especially the sound of a gun being fired.
examples: We heard the report of a gun across the fields.

oewn-06216934-n.learner: What people in general think of a person.
examples: He was a man of good report in the town.

oewn-07234960-n.learner: A written account of how well a student is doing in their work and behaviour.
examples: Her school report said she worked hard in every subject.

oewn-06421395-n.learner: A piece of writing on a subject, especially one written as a set task.
examples: For homework, write a two-page report on a book you have read.

oewn-03243289-n.learner: A low table with one or more mirrors, where you sit while you dress or put on make-up.
examples: She sat at her vanity and brushed her hair.

oewn-06206950-n.learner: The general way in which something tends to grow or develop.
examples: Her career took a new direction after the move.

oewn-06663446-n.learner: Something that gives guidance or advice about what to decide or what to do.
examples: The young manager looked to her for direction.
The direction of a large company takes great skill.

oewn-00816981-n.learner: The act of choosing a course and keeping to it.
examples: In the strong wind, direction of the small boat was almost impossible.

oewn-07184131-n.learner: A formal statement ordering someone to do something.
examples: The court gave a direction that the papers be handed over.

oewn-05712641-n.learner: The putting of your attention or energy on something.
examples: After school she had no direction and drifted from job to job.

oewn-15169138-n.learner: The end or finish of something.
examples: The war put a period to all his plans.

oewn-15272329-n.learner: A unit of time in the earth's history during which a set of rock layers formed.
examples: These fossils come from the Jurassic period.

oewn-15315015-n.learner: The time it takes for something that repeats regularly to go through one full cycle.
examples: This pendulum has a period of two seconds.

oewn-15283092-n.learner: In ice hockey, one of the three parts that a game is divided into.
examples: They scored twice in the second period of the hockey game.
